subtype: Approach: breaking the song or play into small parts [Thinking]
passage:
Monday. Devika stared at the script for the school play. Eight pages of lines, and the show was in ten days. Her stomach flipped. Then she drew three lines with a pencil and cut the role into four scenes. "Just Scene One today." She learned it by evening.

Tuesday. Scene Two was learned, and she ticked the box on her chart.

Wednesday. Naveen, who played her brother, ran lines with her after school. "You know Scenes One to Three already!" Devika grinned. "One scene a day. Tomorrow is the last one." The script did not look so big now.

qa.q: How many scenes did Devika split her part into?
qa.a: Devika split her part into four scenes.

qa.q: What did Devika feel when she first stared at the script?
qa.a: Devika felt nervous and overwhelmed, with a flip in her stomach at eight pages in ten days.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Devika use if she forgets a scene, and why?
qa.a: Devika could record herself reading the lines and listen to it, or practise with a friend. Hearing the words again helps them stay.

qa.q: How might Naveen see Devika's progress?
qa.a: Naveen ran lines with Devika and was impressed that three scenes were already known, so Naveen probably feels reassured about the play.

grounding: A girl in a school play divides her part into four scenes and learns one each day, so the long script feels less scary and she can check her progress.

subtype: Approach: breaking the song or play into small parts [Thinking]
passage: Tenzin, stop hugging that script like it's going to bite you. Sit here with your Ritu Masi. When I was a girl, I was chosen to play the queen in our school play, and my part was pages and pages. The first night I tried to learn it all and cried into my pillow. Then my teacher showed me that the queen appeared in four scenes. So I took a pencil and drew a line under each one. Monday, scene one. Tuesday, scene two. Wednesday, scene three. Thursday, scene four. Every night I ticked the one I'd learnt, and the script got less scary. On Friday I said the whole thing to my mother without looking once.

qa.q: What part did Ritu play in the school play?
How did young Ritu feel the first night she tried to learn the whole part?
qa.a: Young Ritu felt overwhelmed and upset, crying into the pillow.

qa.q: What choice in the story changed things for young Ritu, and why did it work?
qa.a: Splitting the part into four scenes and learning one a day, because each small piece was manageable and the ticks showed progress.

qa.q: How might Ritu's mother have felt on Friday?
qa.a: Ritu's mother was likely proud and surprised to hear the whole part without the script.

grounding: An elder recalls, as a girl in a school play, splitting her part into four scenes and learning one a day so the script felt less scary.

subtype: Approach: breaking the song or play into small parts [Thinking]
passage: Aadhya had eleven days until the annual day play and a part that ran across four scenes. The trouble was, the house was full of relatives for her cousin's engagement, and the only quiet place was the stairwell. On the first evening she sat on the top step and looked at the script, and her heart sank. Then she thought, "Four scenes. Four evenings. One at a time." She folded the pages so only scene one showed. On the phone that night her friend Dilnaz tested her. "Scene one, done?" "Done." On the fourth evening she unfolded all the pages and read the whole part in the noisy stairwell, cousins shouting below, without stumbling.

qa.q: Where was the only quiet place in Aadhya's house?
qa.a: The only quiet place was the stairwell.

qa.q: How did Aadhya feel when she first looked at the whole script?
qa.a: Her heart sank; she felt overwhelmed by the long part in a crowded, noisy house.

qa.q: What else could Aadhya try if relatives filled the stairwell too?
qa.a: She could learn her lines on the way to school or with Dilnaz on the phone, so practice fits around the noise.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Dilnaz?
qa.a: Dilnaz gets a clear way to help, checking one scene at a time, so Dilnaz can see progress and cheer Aadhya on.

grounding: It shows a girl breaking a long school-play part into four scenes and learning one each day, making it less scary and easy to check.
